subject: IM
stem: 45-year-old man has sudden crushing retrosternal pain radiating to left arm, sweaty, ECG shows ST elevation in V2–V4. Onset 90 min ago. Most appropriate next step?
options: A. Oral aspirin only and observe
B. Thrombolysis only if troponin negative
C. Immediate primary percutaneous coronary intervention
explanation: Anterior STEMI <12h: primary PCI is standard if available; give dual antiplatelet + heparin en route. Time is muscle.

subject: IM
stem: 68-year-old with progressive dyspnoea, orthopnoea, bilateral crackles, S3 gallop, ankle oedema. Echo EF 32%. First-line long-term therapy that improves mortality?
options: B. ACE inhibitor + evidence-based beta-blocker + SGLT2 inhibitor
explanation: HFrEF guideline therapy: ACEi/ARNI + beta-blocker (bisoprolol/carvedilol/metoprolol succinate) + MRA + SGLT2i. Diuretics relieve congestion only.

subject: IM
stem: 72-year-old has irregularly irregular pulse, no P waves, variable QRS. CHA2DS2-VASc 4. Management?
explanation: Atrial fibrillation with high stroke risk needs rate/rhythm control plus anticoagulation (DOAC/warfarin), not aspirin alone.

subject: IM
stem: Man develops an itchy, well-demarcated scaly rash confined to the skin under his belt buckle. No vesicles elsewhere, no fever. Most likely diagnosis?
explanation: Recall: rash limited to the contact site (belt buckle → nickel) = allergic contact dermatitis. Confirm with patch testing; avoid the allergen + topical steroid/emollient.

subject: IM
stem: 64-year-old smoker with barrel chest, chronic productive cough, FEV1/FVC 0.58, FEV1 45% predicted. Exacerbation with increased sputum purulence. Best initial approach?
options: B. Short-acting bronchodilators + systemic steroids + antibiotics, target SpO2 88–92%
explanation: COPD exacerbation: bronchodilators, steroids, antibiotics if purulent change, controlled oxygen 88–92% to avoid CO2 retention.

subject: IM
stem: 70-year-old man, day 10 post-op, first mobilisation: sudden unilateral pleuritic chest pain, dyspnoea, diaphoresis, afebrile, self-resolved. Most likely?
explanation: Classic recall pattern: post-op immobilisation + pleuritic pain + dyspnoea = PE until proven otherwise. Needs CT pulmonary angiography + heparin.

subject: IM
stem: Woman has chronic scaly plaques on legs and axillae covering ~10% of body surface; new lesions appear at scratch sites (Koebner phenomenon). No joint pain. Best initial treatment?
options: B. Potent topical steroid + vitamin D analogue (e.g. clobetasol + calcipotriol), consider phototherapy
explanation: Recall: moderate plaque psoriasis (~10% BSA) + Koebner → topical steroid + vitamin D analogue first-line; phototherapy if extensive. Reserve systemic agents for severe/refractory disease; avoid systemic steroids alone (rebound).

subject: IM
stem: 30-year-old with 3-week night sweats, weight loss, upper-lobe cavitary lesion. Next step?
options: B. Sputum AFB smear/culture + GeneXpert, isolate, start RIPE if TB confirmed
explanation: Upper-lobe cavitation + chronic B symptoms = TB. Confirm microbiologically, isolate, RIPE regimen per guidelines.

subject: IM
stem: 19-year-old diabetic with polyuria, vomiting, Kussmaul breathing, glucose 28 mmol/L, ketones strongly positive, pH 7.18. First management?
options: B. IV isotonic fluids + IV insulin infusion + potassium/electrolyte monitoring
explanation: DKA: fluids, insulin, correct K+, treat precipitant (infection). Never oral agents alone.

subject: IM
stem: Patient on sulfonylurea, dose increased, lost 4 kg, lifestyle improved, but HbA1c still 9%. Best next step?
options: B. Stop sulfonylurea and start insulin (add ± metformin)
explanation: Recall pattern: SU failure with HbA1c ≥9% + symptoms/weight loss despite adherence = insulin needed. Don't endlessly up-titrate SU.

subject: IM
stem: Obese type 2 diabetic wants to lose weight and control glucose. Which class most helps weight loss?
explanation: Recall: GLP-1 RAs reduce weight + HbA1c. SU/insulin/TZDs tend to increase weight.

subject: IM
stem: Pregnant woman with Hashimoto on levothyroxine 100 mcg, now TSH high, free T4 normal with hypothyroid symptoms. Next step?
options: B. Increase levothyroxine dose by ~25–30% and recheck TSH
explanation: Pregnancy increases thyroxine needs. High TSH = under-replaced; increase dose. Radioiodine/FNA not indicated here.

subject: IM
stem: 28-year-old woman with tremor, weight loss, heat intolerance, exophthalmos, diffuse goitre. Best initial treatment?
options: B. Beta-blocker for symptoms + carbimazole (antithyroid drug)
explanation: Graves hyperthyroidism: antithyroid (carbimazole/methimazole or PTU in 1st trimester) + propranolol for adrenergic symptoms.

subject: IM
stem: 65-year-old dehydrated after NSAID + diarrhoea: creatinine doubled, K+ 5.8, low urine output. Most likely and first action?
options: A. Pre-renal/AKI – stop nephrotoxin, give isotonic fluids, review meds
D. Immediate dialysis in all cases
explanation: AKI from hypovolaemia + NSAID: stop precipitant, volume resuscitate, monitor UO/electrolytes. Dialysis only for refractory indications.

subject: IM
stem: ECG shows tall peaked T waves, K+ 6.8 mmol/L. First stabilising drug?
options: A. Oral calcium tablet next week
B. IV calcium (gluconate/chloride) + insulin-glucose + shifting measures
explanation: Hyperkalaemia with ECG changes: calcium stabilises myocardium, then insulin-glucose + bicarbonate/salbutamol + binders/dialysis as needed.

subject: IM
stem: Young woman fatigue, pallor, koilonychia, ferritin 6 ng/mL, microcytic anaemia. Best treatment + workup?
options: A. Oral ferrous sulfate + investigate blood loss / hookworm / diet / GI source
explanation: Iron deficiency: replace iron + find cause (menorrhagia, GI loss, parasites, diet). Hookworm is classic EMREE-linked cause.

subject: IM
stem: 22-year-old with sickle-cell disease: severe limb/back pain, no fever, chest clear. Management of vaso-occlusive crisis?
options: A. Fluids + adequate analgesia + oxygen if hypoxic + treat trigger
explanation: VOC: hydration, stepwise analgesia, oxygen, rest, incentive spirometry, screen for ACS/infection.

subject: IM
stem: 70-year-old sudden right hemiparesis + aphasia, onset 2 h ago, CT shows no bleed. Best next step?
options: A. Aspirin only and observe 1 month
B. IV thrombolysis if eligible + stroke unit + urgent workup
explanation: Acute ischaemic stroke <4.5h without bleed: thrombolysis if eligible, plus stroke-unit care, statins, workup. Time-critical.

subject: IM
stem: Generalised tonic-clonic seizure lasting 6 min in ED. First drug?
explanation: Status protocol: benzodiazepine first (lorazepam), then levetiracetam/phenytoin if persists, ABCs + glucose + cause search.

subject: IM
stem: Fever, neck stiffness, photophobia, Kernig positive. After blood cultures, best immediate action?
options: A. Wait for CT before antibiotics 12 h
B. Empirical ceftriaxone (± vancomycin/acyclovir per age) + dexamethasone, then LP
explanation: Suspected bacterial meningitis: don't delay antibiotics for LP/CT. Cultures → immediate empirical antibiotics.

subject: IM
stem: Hypotensive, tachycardic, lactate 4.5, suspected sepsis. Best initial bundle?
options: A. Broad-spectrum antibiotics within 1 h + 30 mL/kg crystalloids + lactate monitoring
explanation: Sepsis-induced hypoperfusion: early antibiotics + aggressive fluids + reassess, then vasopressors if MAP <65.

subject: IM
stem: 24-year-old woman malar rash, arthralgia, oral ulcers, ANA positive, low C3. Most likely and steroid-sparing drug?
options: A. SLE – hydroxychloroquine as backbone (+ steroids/immunosuppressant per severity)
explanation: SLE young woman + malar rash + ANA: hydroxychloroquine for all unless contraindicated; add steroids/immunosuppression for organ disease.

subject: IM
stem: 45-year-old symmetric small-joint polyarthritis, morning stiffness >1 h, anti-CCP positive. First DMARD?
options: A. Methotrexate (with folate) if no contraindication
explanation: RA: early methotrexate + short steroids bridge, then escalate to biologics if target not met.

subject: IM
stem: Acute hot swollen first MTP joint, hyperuricaemia, needle crystals negatively birefringent. Acute treatment?
options: A. Allopurinol during acute attack alone
B. NSAID/colchicine/steroid for acute attack; start urate-lowering later
explanation: Gout flare: anti-inflammatory now; don't start allopurinol alone acutely. Start ULT after flare settles with prophylaxis.
